newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Maastricht airport sees 19pct cargo drop in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Maastricht airport sees 19pct cargo drop in Q1.

text.p: Maastricht Aachen Airport (MAA) saw a sharp decrease in freight traffic in the first quarter of the year, an airport statement said.
Freight volumes for the first three months fell 19 percent compared to the same period in 1996, to 8,800 tonnes.
The main cause was a decline in freight from charter aircraft, which decreased from 3,000 tonnes in the first quarter of last year to 600 tonnes in first quarter 1997.
The sharp decrease in charter traffic was due to the departure of Russian IL-76 aircraft, which had been banned from the airport following environmental pressure from local residents.
Freight from scheduled services increased significantly, up by 24 percent from 6,100 to 7,600 tonnes. Trucked cargo stood at 600 tonnes.
A MAA spokesman said the rise in scheduled cargo traffic had not been enough to make up for the charter shortfall.
Maastricht banned the IL-76 in November last year but prior to that, the southern Dutch airport had already restricted the hours in which these aircraft could land and take off.
In June last year, the airport also requested the IL-76 operators to make a steeper take off to avoid unnecessary noise. But he said the residents were still worried about this type of aircraft.
The spokesman added that he expected the next two quarters would also see a downturn in cargo traffic compared to the equivalent periods ib 1996 because of the departure of the Russian aircraft.
Most of them had switched to Ostend Airport in Belgium, he said.
